page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance alongside average multi-threaded capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded compression workloads, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded performance scales moderately, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores falling into the average tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% of tested systems.

Memory bandwidth tests show average performance across both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also align with mid-tier expectations. For machine learning, the server handles small LLM inference tasks adequately but struggles with medium-sized models, where prompt processing drops to the bottom 10%. This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, mid-sized database hosting, and static web serving, while intensive multi-threaded processing or large-scale AI inference represent clear performance tradeoffs.
